title: 2023 AMC 10B Problem 6
statement: Let \(L_1 = 1,\) \(L_2 = 3,\) and \(L_{n+2} = L_{n+1} + L_n\) for \(n \ge 1.\) How many terms in the sequence \(L_1,\) \(L_2,\) \(L_3,\) \(\ldots,\) \(L_{2023}\) are even?

solutions.text: Track the parities: \(1, 3, 4, 7, 11, 18, \ldots\) run odd, odd, even, then repeat with period \(3.\) So \(L_n\) is even exactly when \(n\) is divisible by \(3.\) Among \(1 \le n \le 2023,\) that’s \(\lfloor \frac{2023}{3} \rfloor = 674\) multiples of \(3.\) Therefore, the answer is E.
hints: Track only the parity of the terms: odd, odd, even, and then it repeats
Even terms occur exactly at positions that are multiples of \(3\)
